questions.q: What's the actual problem this capstone sets out to fix?
options: The same small pieces of logic — group checks, date formatting, reference-field reads — copied and drifting across multiple Business Rules and Client Scripts
ServiceNow instances cannot run GlideRecord queries from Business Rules
Client Scripts are not allowed to call any server-side logic
Script Includes are deprecated in favor of Business Rules
questions.explain: The problem is duplication and drift, not a platform limitation — the same logic rewritten slightly differently in several places.

A GlideRecord object
undefined, because the method body has no return statement yet
A JavaScript error is thrown immediately
questions.explain: A function with no return statement implicitly returns undefined — the method is a stub with a planned signature but no implementation yet.

options: It identifies the class to ServiceNow's internal prototype-based class system and is required on every Script Include built this way
It is optional and only used for code comments
It sets the table the Script Include will query
It makes the Script Include client-callable automatically
questions.explain: The type property names the class for ServiceNow's class system; it's required, but on its own does not make anything client-callable.

questions.q: Why does `isUserInGroup` need special handling that `formatDueDate` and `getReferenceDisplayValue` don't?
options: It needs to be reachable from a Client Script via GlideAjax, which requires extending AbstractAjaxProcessor and exposing a client-callable entry point
It is the only method that returns a string
It is the only method that uses a GlideRecord
It must run slower than the other two methods
questions.explain: Only isUserInGroup is planned to be called from client-side code, which requires the GlideAjax bridge Chapter 4 covered — the other two stay server-side.

questions.q: What does `formatDueDate(glideDateTime)` take as its parameter, per the plan in this lesson?
options: A raw date string like "2026-10-22"
A GlideDateTime object, not a raw string
A GlideRecord pointed at the task table
Nothing — it reads the current date automatically
questions.explain: The planned signature takes a GlideDateTime object so the method can use GlideDateTime's own comparison and display methods, covered in Lesson 31.
